summary: Frontend-only retest of the rewritten ScrollLines component (iteration 8). Verified left-to-right progression, 1:1 scroll movement, 45-degree geometry + rounded (Q) corners, 4-line colors/gaps, z-ordering behind content, footer coverage, and console cleanliness on desktop (1920) and mobile (390x844). Found and fixed one real defect: NaN in the generated path 'd' (zero-length final segment) producing 8 console errors and a truncated path tail on desktop. All requested behaviours now pass.

ui_bugs.issue: FIXED BY TESTER: last waypoint [x,H] coincided exactly with the previous waypoint on desktop (per-cycle y sum == H), so toPath divided by zero length -> 'Q 1635 12148 NaN NaN' in d. Browser logged 8 SVG path errors and truncated the path at y=12124 instead of 12148. Added a consecutive-duplicate-point filter in toPath; now 0 console errors and path ends exactly at docH.

issues: Because the 4 lines are pure horizontal x-offset copies, the perpendicular gap on the 45-degree diagonals is gap/sqrt(2) (~24.7px instead of 35px desktop), so spacing looks slightly tighter on diagonals than on vertical runs. Cosmetic only; bends themselves are smooth and mutually parallel (identical translated shapes). Optional polish: offset along the path normal instead of x.
Lines pop in ~600ms after load (component returns null until measured) - slight visual flash-in on first paint.

action_items: Review/keep the tester's defensive duplicate-point filter in toPath (or make genWaypoints avoid emitting a final duplicate waypoint at y == H).
Optional: normal-offset the 4 copies so diagonal gaps equal vertical gaps.
Optional: render lines immediately (measure synchronously in useLayoutEffect) to remove the ~600ms flash-in.
critical_code_review_comments: toPath had no guard for zero-length segments -> NaN path data; guard added.
genWaypoints per-cycle dy sums to exactly H/n so the trailing pts.push([x,H]) is always a duplicate on desktop; consider dropping it when y >= H.
ResizeObserver on document.body + 600ms timeout works, but setState on every observer fire can cause repeated full-path regeneration on scroll-driven layout changes; consider debouncing.

success_rate.frontend: 100% of requested checks pass after the NaN fix

context_for_next_testing_agent: Measured evidence (desktop 1920, docH 12148): layer is position:absolute, z-index 5, pointer-events none, height == docH; svg getBoundingClientRect().top moves exactly -800px for scrollY 800 (1:1). Mean on-screen line x: 11.3% of viewport at scrollY 0, 51.4% mid-page, 84.8% at page bottom (mobile bottom 90.2%) => left-to-right progression confirmed. Path d contains Q rounded corners; waypoint bends verified |dx|==|dy| (e.g. 96,485 -> 376,765). Horizontal gaps constant 35 desktop / 18 mobile across sampled y's; stroke order #E81C2C,#E81C2C,#C9A227,#C9A227. Z-order verified by thickening strokes to 14px + elementsFromPoint: buttons/cards paint above the lines; footer is position:relative z-10 and covers the lines. 0 console errors on desktop and mobile after the fix. Contact form/tabs were NOT retested per request.
rca_of_the_issue: genWaypoints accumulates a+right+b+back == H/n per cycle, so after n cycles y == H and the appended [x,H] duplicated the previous point. toPath then computed l2 = 0 -> division by zero -> NaN control point, which invalidates the rest of the path in the SVG parser (8 console errors, path visually truncated ~24px early). Mitigation: filter consecutive points closer than 0.5 units before building the path.
